title: Production-Readiness Audit
prompt:
Review settings, secrets, HTTPS, allowed hosts, logging, database, static files, backups, dependency updates, and the deployment checklist.

Submission: a small reviewable artifact, relevant tests, expected outputs, one failure/boundary case, and version/environment notes. Use synthetic data. Django/Python server code is not executed by CodeLeaf browser preview; local or human review is required.
target_skills: Run Django checks using production-like settings.
Document static/media, secrets, database, backup and recovery arrangements.
Record any unresolved issue and owner before release.

starter.content:
python manage.py check --deploy
python manage.py showmigrations
starter.code:
python manage.py check --deploy
python manage.py showmigrations

expected_output: A clean command does not prove production is secure; include a human review of topology and data sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria: The review identifies blocking and nonblocking findings.
Each finding has a verification step and disposition.
State whether verification was local, static, or human-reviewed.
Do not claim a build/deployment or external integration was tested unless it was actually run.
hints: Start with the official deployment checklist.
Confirm DEBUG=False, host policy, HTTPS, secure cookies, secrets, logging and error reporting.
Test restore procedures; a backup not restored is not proven usable.
grading_method: Required-string smoke check plus human review of technical correctness, tests, safe handling, expected result and reproducibility. This does not execute arbitrary Python/Django code.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed after reviewing feedback; the platform backend owns its uniform XP/idempotency rules.
status_note: Practical exercise from Section C of the supplied Django curriculum; content and grading need review before publication.
